sections.label: MCCY and social compact
sections.summary: A motion moves to reduce Head X by $100, citing MCCY's role in safeguarding Singapore's social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum allocated for Head X of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Sir, MCCY shoulders the heavy responsibility of safeguarding the social compact that we have assiduously built in Singapore over the years – the unwavering belief and determination to work together to build towards a collective future regardless of race, language, culture or religion.

sections.label: Racism and social tensions
sections.summary: Singapore has seen racist incidents, discussions on low-wage worker treatment and attitudes towards foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Despite our strong social compact, Singapore has not been spared.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We have seen racist incidents, vocal discussions on the treatment of low-wage workers and attitudes towards foreigners.

sections.label: Minister asked for inclusion strategies
sections.summary: The speaker invites the Minister to share MCCY's strategies for a caring, inclusive society where voices are heard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: And while that will mean that more voices will need to be heard, it will, hopefully, make us a more robust, culturally richer and enduring society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I, therefore, invite the Minister to share MCCY's strategies to ensure that Singapore remains a caring and inclusive society where we care for one another, where everyone's voices are heard and where our shared beliefs unite and drive us as a nation in the years to come.

sections.label: MENDAKI overseas study loan scheme
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MENDAKI can enhance its overseas study loan scheme in loan quantum and by including more new fields.

sections.summary: PERGAS stated on Facebook and Instagram it will form a task force on the LGBT issue, including dialogue with Muslim LGBT members.

sections.summary: GIC and MENDAKI will introduce a new undergraduate scholarship for Singaporean Malay students pursuing a finance career.

sentences.text: Since we set up the Education Trust Fund (ETF) in 2003, MENDAKI has disbursed over $30 million in financial assistance donated by the community to over 130,000 Muslim students.

sentences.text: As MENDAKI celebrates its 40th anniversary, it remains invested in the community's success by looking at more strategic programmes to support our youths to pursue their aspirations and for our workers to strengthen their competencies in a dynamic workforce.

sections.summary: Madrasahs enrol about 380 students yearly at Primary 1, about 50 per cohort leave for national schools, and about one in four graduates become asatizahs.

sentences.text: Every year, the madrasahs collectively enrol about 380 students at Primary 1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But our intent, as Mr Saktiandi may note, is that we have already started with SIA, followed by MiRXES and now GIC.

sections.label: Bequeathing property for religious needs
sections.summary: Bequeathing property for religious needs and society is a 1,400-year culture, accumulating almost $800 billion worth of assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This culture of bequeathing your property to benefit yourself for your religious needs – but more importantly, to benefit society for the long term – is a culture that we have had for 1,400 years and we have had it in Singapore when Muslim Singaporeans had become wealthy during the early days of our colonisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: And in bequeathing these properties and, actually, in enhancing these properties alone, we have managed to accumulate something like almost $800 billion worth of assets.

sections.label: Asatizah salary review and community funding
sections.summary: Speaker calls for community benefit, notes an asatizah salary review announced in early 2020, and thanks mosque and madrasah communities for responding without MUIS mandates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: And I am calling them: it is great that you are benefiting yourself and your children; just think about benefiting the community and for the future.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: I note that we are going to have a salary review of the asatizahs and I also realised that it was announced somewhere in early 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For MUIS, we can only be in control of the sectors under our care and that have to do with our madrasahs and mosques.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I am very thankful that the mosque community, the madrasah community have responded without us making it compulsory or mandated through MUIS' instructions.

sections.label: Generosity for asatizah salaries
sections.summary: Speaker says asatizahs should be treated more generously, with the salary review identifying gaps and community wealth funding religious needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Therefore, for our asatizahs, we should be more generous and not hold back this amount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: There is no benchmark for this, but, over the long term, we hope that the review on the salaries will tell us exactly where we are, what the gaps are, and, more importantly, how to get the funds to fund this gap, and here is where we will need to rely on the wealth and generosity of our own community to fund our own religious needs.

sections.label: FITRAH, UPLIFT and ComLink coordination
sections.summary: Speaker assures Ms Nadia Samdin that programme coordination continues, with FITRAH family support under UPLIFT and ComLink, and post-release support needed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Part of the effort of helping FITRAH families will be the effort of UPLIFT, part of the effort will be under ComLink.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: So, the coordination effort is being worked on and, certainly, we agree that it is not just while the inmate is incarcerated, support must continue to be given even after they have been released so that they see stabilisation has been achieved while they are incarcerated.

sections.label: Community Dispute Resolution Framework
sections.summary: The Community Dispute Resolution Framework has been a useful and complementary tool to improve community dispute management.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: To this end, the Community Dispute Resolution Framework has been a useful and complementary tool to improve community dispute management.

sections.label: Noise feedback and CDRT applications
sections.summary: HDB reported around 38,400 noise-related feedback cases last year, a 25% rise from 2020, while CDRT saw higher applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, last year, HDB reported around 38,400 cases of noise-related feedback, a 25% increase from 2020, while the Community Dispute Resolution Tribunal (CDRT) also saw higher applications.

sections.label: CMC effectiveness and mandating mediation
sections.summary: Speaker asks about CMC's effectiveness and mandating mediation, citing constituents who found CDRT engagement difficult, long and adversarial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share more on CMC's effectiveness and will the Government consider mandating mediation for community disputes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My constituents gave feedback that those who have engaged with the CDRT have not found it to be easy, as they faced long battles which are often adversarial in nature, usually as a result of counter parties raising evidence or allegations haphazardly during proceedings.

sections.label: CMC mediation cases declined
sections.summary: Of 735 yearly CMC cases, 70% did not proceed to mediation, mainly because parties declined or did not respond, prompting a question on compulsory attendance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Of the average of 735 cases per year registered at the CMC, 70% did not progress to mediation, mainly because one or both parties declined or did not respond to the invitation to mediate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, once the CMC assesses a case to be suitable for mediation, can attendance of both parties be made compulsory?

sections.label: CDRT web portal evidence
sections.summary: A question asks whether CDRT can update its processes to allow evidence uploads on the web portal and make the process more user-friendly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the CDRT update its processes to allow evidence to be uploaded on the web portal instead and to make the whole process more user-friendly for the layman?

sections.label: CDRT order breaches and mediation
sections.summary: Questions ask what Courts or complainants did when parties breached tribunal orders, and whether CDRT mediation can be made compulsory amid more neighbourly disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Also, what actions, if any, have our Courts or complainants taken when offending parties, even after the tribunal order, still continue to perpetrate and breach the order?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I wish to also ask MCCY to share if there are plans to better ensure the more effective and efficient resolution of CDRT complaints as there are more situations of work from home and resulting in more neighbourly disputes and some of these disputes cannot be resolved via the voluntary mediation route via community mediation and whether such mediation, moving forward, can be made compulsory?

sections.label: Race and religion Police cases

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: In 2020, MHA spotted a spike in race and religion-related Police cases.

sections.label: NVPC 2021 volunteerism survey
sections.summary: NVPC's 2021 survey found regular volunteerism fell amid COVID-19 measures, with 48% volunteering less since DORSCON Orange, while online volunteering and donations rose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: The findings of the Individual Giving Survey by the National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre (NVPC) in 2021 showed that regular volunteerism took a hit mainly due to the measures implemented to curb the spread of COVID-19, with nearly half of the volunteers saying that they have volunteered less since DORSCON Orange was alerted on 7 February 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: NVPC polled more than 2,000 people between 8 April and 17 September 2021 for the study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: They noted that 48% of volunteers volunteered less since DORSCON Orange was declared on 7 February 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: Notably, online volunteering sign-ups in Singapore saw a 29% increase and online donation rose 37%, compared to pre-pandemic levels.

sections.label: Youth civic participation plans
sections.summary: Questions ask about plans for more civic participation opportunities for youths on national interest topics and support for their ground-up social and environmental actions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share its plans to provide even more opportunities for the civic participation of our youths from diverse backgrounds on topics of national interest, such as the review of our nationally determined contributions and other sustainability goals?

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Additionally, what are the Government's plans to support our youths in taking ground-up actions on social and environmental causes they are passionate about?

sections.label: MCCY engagement and vision
sections.summary: Asks how conversations became concrete action and how MCCY will give Singaporeans chances to contribute ideas toward a caring, just and equal society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How have these conversations translated into concrete and measurable action?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How will MCCY continue to provide Singaporeans with opportunities to contribute ideas and work towards our vision of a caring, just and equal society?

sections.label: A Tapestry of Sacred Music
sections.summary: Cites A Tapestry of Sacred Music, a month-long Esplanade festival taking place this month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One example is A Tapestry of Sacred Music, which is a month-long festival at the Esplanade taking place, in fact, this month.

sections.label: March On and arts resilience
sections.summary: Notes the March On festival at the Esplanade and asks how MCCY will build back the arts and culture community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My second question is that the Arts and Culture Resilience Package was much appreciated by our community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Going forward, to ensure a vibrant, resilient ecosystem for the arts and culture sector, how will MCCY plan to build back this community to co-create new innovative and sustainable models together with actors across the value chain, in this sector?

sections.label: ACRP funding and opportunities
sections.summary: States the ACRP was enhanced with $20 million in March 2021, totalling $75 million over two years, and created over 13,000 opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: The ACRP was enhanced with $20 million in March 2021, bringing it to a total of $75 million over two years.

sentences.text: At the Committee of Supply last year, MCCY had shared that the first tranche of the ACRP created over 13,000 work and training opportunities, of which, 5,000 were for self-employed practitioners.

sections.summary: Notes MCCY said a CMF review would be conducted and that Finance Minister Lawrence Wong announced a top-up in Budget 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: This top-up was announced by Finance Minister Lawrence Wong in his Budget 2022 Statement.

sections.label: Hawker Culture UNESCO inscription

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: One example is the successful inscription of our Hawker Culture on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) of Humanity.

sections.label: Support for arts cultural workers
sections.summary: Asks how the Government helps self-employed arts and cultural workers sustain livelihoods and revitalise Singapore's arts scene.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: It is inevitable that they were hit harder during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: How is the progress so far and how is the Government helping arts and cultural workers to hone their craft while sustaining their livelihood?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: How will the Government revitalise the diverse cultural and arts scenes in Singapore and ensure that Singapore continues to have our unique position in the world?

sections.summary: States that the arts and culture sector has been hard hit and severely disrupted by the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Yet, the arts and culture sector has been hard hit by the pandemic and has been severely disrupted by it.

sections.summary: Asks MCCY for strategies, ACRP impact updates and plans on manpower and digitalisation for arts organisations and freelancers.

sentences.text: What are MCCY's strategies to revitalise the arts and culture sectors and ensure that our organisations and freelancers are well-positioned to thrive in the new normal?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can MCCY also elaborate on its strategies to provide more inclusiveness through sports in the next phase of the Disability Sports Master Plan?

sentences.text: Can MCCY provide an update on how Team Singapore athletes are progressing in their preparation for the major games in 2022 and beyond?

sections.summary: Asks about MCCY efforts to rally Singaporeans' support and platforms for Team Singapore athletes to connect and inspire.

sentences.text: Can MCCY share its efforts to rally Singaporeans to show their support for Team Singapore and also to provide platforms for Team Singapore athletes to connect with and inspire Singaporeans?

sentences.text: That was the biggest mass sports event in Singapore since the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: What are the Ministry's plans to restore national sports participation and reintroduce mass sports events in a safe manner?

sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to elaborate on inclusive sports strategies and opportunities for aspiring para-athletes to compete.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Can the Ministry elaborate on its strategies to provide more inclusive opportunities through sports in our Disability Sports Master Plan?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: How can we provide more opportunities for our aspiring para-athletes to pursue sports at a competitive level?

sections.label: Singapore Together Alliances for Action
sections.summary: 31 Singapore Together Alliances for Action involving over 34,000 individuals were formed to address key themes.

sentences.text: In this vein, 31 Singapore Together Alliances for Action (AfAs), involving over 34,000 individuals from the people, private and public sectors were formed to address key themes, for example, the AfA on Lower-Wage Workers, which spearheaded eight ground-up projects to uplift lower-wage workers.

sections.label: Small Business Recovery Grant
sections.summary: The Government will introduce the Small Business Recovery Grant and extend the COVID-19 Recovery Grant to end-2022.

sentences.text: The Government will introduce the Small Business Recovery Grant (SBRG) and will also extend the COVID-19 Recovery Grant (CRG) to end-2022.

sections.label: Support for arts organisations

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The ACRP and broad-based support schemes supported over 900 arts and culture organisations.

sections.label: Venue Hire Subsidy for arts
sections.summary: The Venue Hire Subsidy was introduced to defray performance costs, supporting over 1,700 live performances and cultural events in 2020 and 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To support our arts groups, we introduced the Venue Hire Subsidy (VHS) to defray performance costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This encouraged the resumption of activities and also brought back vibrancy to our arts and cultural scene, with more than 1,700 live performances and other cultural events supported in 2020 and 2021.

sections.label: ACRP digitalisation projects supported
sections.summary: Over 1,500 digitalisation projects were supported under the ACRP through the Digitalisation Fund, including the Digital Presentation Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Over 1,500 digitalisation projects were supported under the ACRP through the Digitalisation Fund, including the Digital Presentation Grant (DPG).

sections.label: Additional $12 million arts support
sections.summary: An additional $12 million will be provided in FY2022 in continued support of arts and culture practitioners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To build on the gains that we have made, we will provide an additional $12 million in FY2022 in continued support of our arts and culture practitioners.

sections.label: CMF grants to arts charities
sections.summary: Arts and heritage charities received over $300 million in CMF grants, reflecting donations catalysed by the CMF since its inception.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Arts and heritage charities received over $300 million in CMF grants, reflecting donations catalysed by the CMF since its inception.

sections.summary: A top-up of $150 million into the CMF aims to sustain giving momentum and encourage charities to keep fundraising and develop donor relationships.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: There will, therefore, be a top-up of $150 million into the CMF.

sections.label: Padang National Monument gazetting
sections.summary: NHB is working towards gazetting the Padang as a National Monument on National Day later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: NHB is working towards the gazetting of the Padang as a National Monument on National Day later this year.

sections.label: ActiveSG digital content and SRP
sections.summary: ActiveSG Circle has developed over 3,000 hours of digital content since 2020, and the Sports Resilience Package was enhanced to $75 million last year.

sentences.text: The ActiveSG Circle has partnered stakeholders to develop more than 3,000 hours of digital content since 2020 and, to date, has accumulated a viewership of 67 million, with five million unique visitors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We have also been nudging digital production and innovation through the Sports Resilience Package (SRP), which was enhanced to a total of $75 million last year.

sections.label: Sports as social glue
sections.summary: Sports bring people together, and $20 million will be committed to the Bring Sport Back programme in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Like arts, sports are a social "glue" that brings us together, as we cheer on our athletes fighting hard for Singapore, or as we develop friendships by simply engaging in a game or two on the field or on the court.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will commit $20 million to our Bring Sport Back programme in 2022.

sections.label: Para Sport Academy launch
sections.summary: SportSG will introduce the Para Sport Academy under ActiveSG's Academies and Clubs for persons with disabilities to pursue competitive sport.

sentences.text: First, SportSG will introduce the Para Sport Academy, under ActiveSG's Academies and Clubs, to create more opportunities for persons with disabilities to pursue their sporting ambition at a competitive level.

sections.label: SportCares support programmes

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: SportCares will also roll out a mentoring programme and will also offer bursaries, scholarships and internships for youths from disadvantaged backgrounds.

sections.label: Workgroup on IRCCs
sections.summary: A Workgroup has been formed to review refreshing IRCCs to strengthen racial and religious harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To this end, we have formed a Workgroup to review how we can refresh our IRCCs to continue strengthening our racial and religious harmony.

sections.label: Smart RC/RN rollout

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The pilot centres allowed for enhanced use, fostered a greater sense of coming together and community and belonging for the neighbourhoods involved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will progressively roll out the pilot across more RC centres in the second half of 2022 to take advantage of some of the gains we have seen from the pilot.

sections.label: Interagency workgroup reviewing framework
sections.summary: An interagency workgroup has been reviewing this framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: An interagency workgroup has been reviewing this framework.

sentences.text: For every 10 cases that go before the CMC, 8.8 of them are resolved.

sections.label: Mandating mediation before CDRT claims

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We are also studying possible mechanisms for a CMC settlement agreement to be registered as an order of Court.

sections.label: CDRT claims and process changes

sections.label: MCCY sectors emerging from pandemic

sentences.text: For example, our national cultural institutions have adopted the Tripartite Standards on Contracting with SEPs since 2018.

sections.label: TPD visitors and Kampong Java spaces

sentences.text: Following NHB's consultations with a diverse range of stakeholders that include insights from our museum community, youth, creatives, heritage societies and heritage business owners, NHB is drawing up plans for Our SG Heritage Plan 2.0.

sections.label: Unleash the Roar football project

sections.label: Additional funds for Team Singapore

sentences.text: As Team Singapore takes the stage multiple times this year, I would like to ask for additional funds to be allocated to enable our Team Singapore athletes a fair shot at preparing, qualifying and competing at these major international competitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: One, develop a framework for licensing and compulsory registration for all sports coaches and instructors; and two, extend the registration to administrators and volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can MCCY share its future plans for this Fund, so that we can continue to encourage a spirit of giving towards high-performance sports in Singapore?

sections.label: Bahrain Asian Youth Para Games medals

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: For the Bahrain Asian Youth Para Games, Singapore sent 13 athletes and the amazing team made the nation proud by bringing back five gold, three silver and two bronze medals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: There is a Disability Sports Master Plan in place setting the roadmap for various initiatives.

sections.label: Youth unemployment rate figures

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Annual average resident youth unemployment rate hit 10.6%, 1.8% higher than during the 2009 global financial crisis and 1.3% higher than during the 2003 SARS pandemic.

sections.label: Mentors in growth sectors

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Mentors, especially in growth sectors, can play a meaningful role in this effort.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I support the efforts of Mentoring Alliance Singapore and oversee the youth empowerment and mentoring programmes under M3.

sections.label: Training mentors from growing industries
sections.summary: Given the post-pandemic economic evolution, it is timely and more urgent to train people from various growing industries to become mentors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Given the current evolution of the economy post-pandemic, it is timely, in fact, more urgent now, to train people from various growing industries to become mentors.

sections.label: Strategic mentoring framework for youths
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MCCY can develop a more strategic and current mentoring framework for youths, including emotional development and resilience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: There are a lot more programmes and opportunities now, compared to the time when I was in school.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We could continue to improve on this by creating an ecosystem and culture of mentoring in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Aside from educational development and career prospects, it is important to also look into the emotional development and resilience of youths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We should garner the insights and build that in as part of the training of mentors or mentoring programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I, therefore, hope that MCCY can look at efforts to develop a more strategic and current mentoring framework for our youths.

sections.label: Greener sustainable sports ecosystem plans
sections.summary: The question asks MCCY to elaborate on its plans to ensure a greener and more sustainable sports ecosystem.

sentences.text: Chairman, as part of the Government's overall efforts to secure a sustainable future for Singapore, can MCCY elaborate on its plans to ensure a greener and more sustainable sports ecosystem?

sections.summary: The question asks about plans for Sport SG to roll out green concepts to other sports centres and how MCCY intends to involve the sports community, Singaporeans and private sector partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Are there any other plans for Sport SG to roll out similar green concepts to other sports centres across Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How else does MCCY intend to involve the sports community, Singaporeans and partners from the private sectors to co-create solutions for sustainability and play a part in these efforts?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Can MCCY share what is done to support youths' concerns and needs in their key priority areas?

sentences.text: Chairman, a young resident of mine, only 23 years old, committed suicide in June last year.

sentences.text: Singapore established a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Colombia, and a partnership with venture capital (VC) firm, Latin Leap, to promote closer collaboration with companies in Latin America, especially in areas of artificial intelligence, fintech and sustainability.

sections.label: Youth Corps Internship Scheme
sections.summary: At the height of COVID-19, the Youth Corps Internship Scheme provided over 700 youths with internships since September 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: At the height of COVID-19, we rolled out our Youth Corps Internship Scheme, which provided more than 700 youths with internship experiences since September 2020.

sections.label: Mentoring Alliance for Action
sections.summary: The Mentoring Alliance for Action was launched to build a mentoring culture for youths in transitions, with over 1,000 volunteer mentors via WeConnect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Mentoring will play a key part in the upstream.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: That is why we launched our Mentoring Alliance for Action (AfA) last year, to build a stronger mentoring culture in Singapore, especially for youths undergoing life's many transitions, be it from school-to-work, or when switching careers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Through WeConnect, you can connect with a pool of over 1,000 volunteer mentors, which is growing, coming from companies like P&G, Unilever and Meta.

sections.label: Youth mental well-being projects
sections.summary: Over 1,500 individuals have started more than 20 ground-up projects to support youths' mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Since then, more than 1,500 individuals, comprising youths, parents, caregivers, mental health professionals, have started more than 20 ground-up projects to support youths' mental well-being.

sections.label: Youths tackling societal issues
sections.summary: Since 2019, over 700 youths formed more than 170 project teams to tackle societal issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Since 2019, we have worked with over 700 youths, who have formed more than 170 project teams, to tackle societal issues, ranging from environment and sustainability, to support for vulnerable groups.

sections.label: Skilio youth portfolio access
sections.summary: With YAC's support, Skilio expanded offerings, and over 5,000 students across 11 schools and organisations have joined.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Thus far, over 5,000 students across 11 different schools and organisations have joined Skilio, with the potential to scale.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Combined with locale-based offerings, YCS offers a total of 7,500 opportunities where any youth with a heart to serve can step forward to bridge gaps in our society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We will highlight important norms and values that should guide our conversations and create spaces for respectful and deep dialogue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Together, 20 representatives from 15 different community groups, corporations and grassroot organisations will co-create and drive these projects.

sections.label: Building Singapore's shared future
sections.summary: The passage calls on the current generation to build on past foundations and create new bridges to the world and one another.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Great cities, including strong bridges, were not built in a day nor by a single person or group.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This mirrors the words that our former President, Mr Yusof Ishak said more than 50 years ago, "In every brick, stone, stool that makes up Singapore, there is contained the effort and energies of generations of men, starting with the early immigrants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The whole fabric of Singapore society is woven out of the thread of human effort, labour and purpose." As we embark on the next arc of our Singapore story, it is now our time, our turn, to build on these foundations and create new bridges to the world, towards our shared future and with one another.

sentences.text: First, we are greening our sport infrastructure like the upcoming Punggol Regional Sport Centre in 2024 and the Kallang Alive Precinct into a sports and recreational Green Mark District.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: SportSG will ensure that all its supported events attain green certification by 2023.

sections.label: Extending Charities Capability Fund
sections.summary: The Charities Capability Fund will be extended from FY2022 to FY2026, as shared by the Finance Minister.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As shared by the Finance Minister, we will extend the Charities Capability Fund from FY2022 to FY2026.

sections.label: PwD sports participation growth

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The number of PwDs participating in sports has grown from one in three in 2016 to one in two today.

sentences.text: In summary, the DSMP has benefited more than 18,000 persons with disabilities to date.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will continue to do this and more.

sections.summary: The Government spends more than $70 million yearly on high-performance sports, over and above $90 million on sports infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Each year, the Government spends more than $70 million in high-performance sports, over and above the $90 million on sports infrastructure.

sentences.text: As previously announced by the Finance Minister, we are extending the $50 million OTSF Matching Grant for an additional five years until FY2026 and to cover more areas of high-performance sports support.

sections.label: Unleash the Roar football partnerships
sections.summary: Singapore works with LaLiga and Borussia Dortmund, trains over 300 coaches and MOE teachers, and will launch a scholarship.

sentences.text: To go far, we must work with the right partners.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: First, we will launch the "Unleash the Roar!" scholarship to nurture young talents later this year.

sections.label: YCCI programme start and overseas stints

sentences.text: The YCCI programme is one of many different programmes and it is starting in the second quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Pre-COVID-19, we sent about four to five thousand youths every year for two-week community service stints with overseas youth organisations.

sections.label: Asia Exposure Ready Programme

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The other programme is the Asia Exposure Ready Programme (AEP), which will expand support to travel-based programmes, when it is possible, for a more experiential and more community-based experience for youths overseas.

sections.label: Pathways for athletes with disabilities
sections.summary: On Mr Mark Chay's point about potential pathways, the intent is to put them on the same platform as able-bodied athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As to Mr Mark Chay's point about what are the potential pathways, we intend to put them on the same platform as the able-bodied athletes.

sections.label: Optimal, fair, relevant space usage
sections.summary: Given land scarcity, spaces should be used optimally and efficiently, with fair access, turnover for new groups, and continued relevance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Given Singapore's land scarcity, we want to ensure optimal usage and efficiency in usage; second, we want to ensure that there is fair access because we have new and younger groups coming through and we want to ensure that, for the space, there is sufficient turnover, so that they can also occupy the spaces and there are opportunities for these new growing groups to incubate and experiment; and, finally, we want these spaces to continue to remain relevant.

sections.label: Real estate space for arts
sections.summary: Over the last 10 years, real estate space dedicated to arts users grew by about 35% in absolute terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If you take just the real estate purposes, over the last 10 years, we have grown it by about 35% in terms of absolute real estate space dedicated to arts users.

sections.label: Reimagining old terrace properties
sections.summary: Terrace properties were reimagined into independent affordable spaces for experimental and incubatory arts companies, to use spaces fairly and efficiently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It used to be terrace properties, so, a little bit grungy, a little bit rundown, but quite perfect and ideal for arts spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, we reimagined the space, thought about how these can become independent affordable spaces for, again, experimental and incubatory arts companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These are some examples of the thinking in terms of how we can expand on existing spaces, old spaces, to bring them into new ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And also, ultimately, use the spaces fairly and efficiently and ensuring that, as and when we have new companies, new ideas, new forms of art coming through, they will also have their space in the sun and be able to develop.
